title: threshold-exporter chart values — key sets
description: Refuses a key this chart does not have at `helm template` / `helm install` / `helm upgrade`, instead of letting it be silently ignored (#1425: `--set thresholdConfig.existingConfigMap=…` against a chart without the switch rendered BOTH ConfigMaps and exit 0). Same shape as helm/tenant-api/values.schema.json (#1594): only KEY SETS are constrained (additionalProperties:false on the root and on every fixed-shape block); free-form maps (tenants, defaults, state_filters, annotations, resources, probes, serviceMonitor labels) stay open, and leaves are deliberately untyped — the templates' {{ fail }} guards carry the type checks because their messages say WHY (existingConfigMap, max_metrics_per_tenant, optional_overrides). Nulls stay legal wherever values.yaml documents them (`startupProbe: null`, `httpGet: null`, `release: null`). Held key-for-key equal to values.yaml by tests/helm/test_threshold_exporter_values_schema.py.

global.description: Helm's own key, injected when this chart is used as a subchart. Not read by any template.

enabled.description: Helm's subchart condition convention: an umbrella chart's `dependencies[].condition: threshold-exporter.enabled` passes this key down. Not read by any template.

defaults.description: Open map: the registry-generated keys plus any a custom rule pack adds.

optional_overrides.description: Typed by the guard in templates/configmap.yaml (a list of key names).

max_metrics_per_tenant.description: Typed by the guard in templates/configmap.yaml (integer, or null for the built-in 500).

state_filters.description: Open map of state filter definitions.

existingConfigMap.description: Typed by the guard in templates/deployment.yaml (a ConfigMap name).

labels.description: Open map; `release: null` drops the default label.

startupProbe.description: Kubernetes Probe, passed through; null omits it.
